summary: Ways to move around a site or an app, and how the navigation itself behaves and moves.

entries.what: The header stays at the top while the page scrolls, so navigation and the main action stay at hand.
entries.use_when: Long pages, documentation, shops, apps where the main action or search lives in the header.
entries.avoid_when: Short pages; phone screens where it eats more than about 10 % of the height.
entries.build: position: sticky; top: 0 on the header, a z-index from the scale (--z-sticky), scroll-margin-top on anchors equal to its height plus 16 px, and focus never hidden under it.
checks: premium-craft: anchors, z-index scale, focus not hidden

label.fr: En-tête qui se cache au défilement

entries.what: The header slides away when the user scrolls down and comes back as soon as they scroll up.
entries.use_when: Reading pages and phone screens where height is precious.
entries.avoid_when: App screens where the header holds tools used all the time.
entries.build: Compare scroll positions in a passive scroll listener or with an IntersectionObserver sentinel; translateY(-100%) with a 200 ms ease-out transition, never animate top. With prefers-reduced-motion: no movement, a plain state change.

entries.what: A tall header with a large logo becomes a compact bar after the first screen.
entries.use_when: Brand sites, restaurants, hotels, portfolios that open on a large header.
entries.avoid_when: Apps and dashboards.
entries.build: Two states switched by a class from an IntersectionObserver on the hero; animate transform and opacity only, or use a scroll-driven animation (animation-timeline: scroll()).

entries.what: The header sits transparent over a full-width image or video and becomes solid when the page scrolls.
entries.use_when: Hotels, travel, restaurants, luxury, events with a strong opening image.
entries.avoid_when: When the text over the image cannot keep 4.5:1 contrast.
entries.build: A gradient scrim behind the header text for contrast; the solid state switches at the end of the hero.

entries.what: A wide panel under a top-level item that shows grouped links, sometimes with an image or a short description each.
entries.use_when: Sites with many sections: shops, SaaS with several products, public services, universities.
entries.avoid_when: Fewer than about 12 destinations: a simple menu is faster.
entries.build: Opens on click (and on hover with a 150 to 300 ms intent delay), closes with Esc and on outside click, keyboard order follows the columns; disclosure button with aria-expanded.

entries.what: A button opens a panel from the side or the top with the whole navigation, on phones.
entries.use_when: Any public site on phone with more than four or five destinations.
entries.avoid_when: Apps with three to five main destinations: a bottom tab bar is faster to reach.
entries.build: A real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls, focus moved into the panel and trapped, Esc and a visible close button, scroll of the page locked, overscroll-behavior: contain. Slide 250 ms ease-out, exit 20 % shorter. With prefers-reduced-motion: no movement, a plain state change.

entries.what: The menu covers the whole screen with large links, often animated in one after the other.
entries.use_when: Agencies, studios, portfolios, fashion and luxury brands where the menu is part of the show.
entries.avoid_when: Sites people use to get something done quickly.
entries.build: Same accessibility as the drawer; links staggered by 30 to 50 ms; the whole menu readable at 200 % zoom.

entries.what: Three to five main destinations in a bar at the bottom of the phone screen, within reach of the thumb.
entries.use_when: Apps and web apps on phone with three to five main sections.
entries.avoid_when: Actions (a tab never starts an action), more than five destinations, desktop widths (use a rail or a sidebar).
entries.build: Each tab is a link with an icon and a label; the selected one is marked by more than colour; safe-area padding at the bottom (env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); the bar stays visible except in modals.

entries.what: A pill or underline behind the selected tab slides to the newly chosen tab instead of jumping.
entries.use_when: Tab bars, segmented controls, filters, pricing toggles.
entries.avoid_when: Nothing: it is the safest of the tab animations.
entries.build: One indicator moved between tabs: Motion layoutId, a View Transition with view-transition-name, or a clip-path on a duplicated active tab list. About 250 ms with an ease-in-out curve (it is a move); on React Native, animate translateX and width, not scaleX, so the corners stay round; haptic feedback on the press. With prefers-reduced-motion: no movement, a plain state change.

entries.what: The icon of the chosen tab lifts slightly and switches from outline to filled.
entries.use_when: Bottom tab bars with outline icons.
entries.avoid_when: Icon sets without a filled variant (do not fake it with a heavier stroke).
entries.build: Swap the outline and filled icon with opacity, a scale from 0.9 and blur(2px) together, under 200 ms; translateY(-2px) at most for the lift. With prefers-reduced-motion: no movement, a plain state change.

entries.what: Only the selected tab shows its label: its pill widens to reveal the name while the others show icons only.
entries.use_when: Bottom bars with four or five tabs and short names.
entries.avoid_when: Long or translated names that change the width a lot; users who need labels to recognise icons (keep labels on all tabs then).
entries.build: Animate the pill with transform (scaleX on a background layer) or a layout animation, never width on the text itself; the label fades in after the pill, 200 to 250 ms total. With prefers-reduced-motion: no movement, a plain state change.

entries.what: A disc carrying the selected icon jumps into a notch cut in the bar above the chosen tab.
entries.use_when: Playful consumer apps where the bar is part of the identity.
entries.avoid_when: Work apps and anything used many times a day: it is slow and draws the eye at every change.
entries.build: SVG path for the bar with the notch moved by transform, the disc on an arc (offset-path or two transforms); keep it under 300 ms. With prefers-reduced-motion: no movement, a plain state change.

entries.what: The bar bulges under the chosen tab like a liquid, then settles.
entries.use_when: Consumer apps with a playful or organic identity.
entries.avoid_when: Work apps, frequent switching, low-end phones.
entries.build: SVG path morph (Motion or a spring on the control points) or a gooey filter (blur plus contrast); test the frame rate on a low-end phone. With prefers-reduced-motion: no movement, a plain state change.
entries.cost: high effort, heavy on low-end phones

entries.what: Small bubbles rise from the chosen tab and pop.
entries.use_when: Games, kids' apps, celebrations; once, not at every switch.
entries.avoid_when: Anything used for work, and repeated switching.
entries.build: A few absolutely positioned circles animated with transform and opacity, removed after the animation; or a Lottie or Rive file. With prefers-reduced-motion: no movement, a plain state change.
entries.cost: decorative; flagged as motion without information on frequent actions

entries.what: A narrow vertical bar of icons with labels on the side of the screen, between a tab bar and a full sidebar.
entries.use_when: Tablets and medium widths; apps with three to seven destinations.
entries.avoid_when: Phones (use the bottom bar).
entries.build: Material 3 navigation rail pattern: 80 px wide, icon with label, selected state with an indicator; switch from the bottom bar at about 600 px.

entries.what: A persistent column of navigation on the left of an app, often collapsible.
entries.use_when: Apps and dashboards with more than five sections or nested sections.
entries.avoid_when: Marketing pages.
entries.build: 5 to 8 top-level items, groups with headings, collapsible to a rail with its state remembered; keyboard shortcut to toggle.

entries.what: Ctrl or Cmd + K opens a search box that finds pages, records and actions.
entries.use_when: Apps with many screens or records, documentation, developer tools.
entries.avoid_when: Small sites with a few pages.
entries.build: A dialog with a combobox (role=combobox, listbox of results), arrow keys, Enter, Esc; recent items first; the shortcut shown with the platform's symbols. Libraries: cmdk (MIT).

entries.what: A search field that finds content across the site, with results as you type or on a results page.
entries.use_when: Documentation, shops, blogs, public services, any site with more than a few dozen pages.
entries.avoid_when: Small showcase sites.
entries.build: Static sites: Pagefind (MIT) indexes at build time; apps: the database's full-text search. Debounce 250 to 300 ms, cancel the previous request, highlight the match.

entries.what: A trail of links showing where the page sits in the hierarchy.
entries.use_when: Shops, documentation, public services, deep hierarchies.
entries.avoid_when: Flat sites of one or two levels.
entries.build: <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> with an ordered list, the current page with aria-current="page"; BreadcrumbList structured data for search engines.

entries.what: A list of the page's headings beside or above long content, with the current section highlighted.
entries.use_when: Articles, documentation, legal pages, long guides.
entries.avoid_when: Short pages.
entries.build: Built from the h2 and h3; current section from an IntersectionObserver; sticky on desktop, collapsed at the top on phone.

entries.what: A button that appears after some scrolling and brings the user back to the top.
entries.use_when: Long pages: articles, documentation, long lists.
entries.avoid_when: Pages under about three screens.
entries.build: Appears after about two screens, a real link to #top or a button that moves focus to the top; smooth scroll only without prefers-reduced-motion.

entries.what: A round button fixed in a corner that opens contact options (chat, phone, email, WhatsApp).
entries.use_when: Local services, restaurants, real estate, shops where a quick question leads to a sale.
entries.avoid_when: Apps and dashboards; pages where it covers content or a cookie banner on phone.
entries.build: Fixed bottom right with safe-area margins, never over the main action or form fields; a real button with a name; links tel:, mailto: or a chat. Hide it while the keyboard is open.

entries.what: One round button for the screen's main creation action (new message, new task), floating above the content.
entries.use_when: Phone apps where one creation action dominates.
entries.avoid_when: Screens with several equal actions; desktop (put the action in the toolbar).
entries.build: Material 3 FAB: 56 dp, bottom right, above the tab bar; extended FAB with a label when space allows.

entries.what: The first keyboard stop is a link that jumps over the menu to the main content.
entries.use_when: Every page with a menu or header before the content.
entries.avoid_when: Nothing: it is a rule, offered here for completeness.
entries.build:
Skip to content as the first element, visible on focus;
.
